muc.title: A million robots
muc.text: In 2025, Amazon put its one millionth robot into its warehouses. They move among people and shelves without crashing thanks to the three eyes you've just learned about.

muc.title: Robots read codes on the floor
muc.text: Shelf-carrying robots read codes stuck to the floor with a camera on their underside to know which square they're on. Robots that roam freely between aisles use LiDAR to map the space and avoid people.

muc.title: A forklift's stop zone
muc.text: A self-driving forklift uses LiDAR to draw a no-entry zone around itself. At 2 meters per second it needs 2.2 meters to stop, so the zone is set at 3.3 meters, and the forklift stops when someone steps inside.

muc.title: Cameras at the intersection
muc.text: At intersections, AI cameras count motorbikes and cars in each direction to extend the green light for the busier side, and read the plates of cars that run a red light.

muc.title: Radar speed guns
muc.text: Speed guns use Doppler radar like in part 2, turning the frequency shift into kilometers per hour, even at night or in the rain.

muc.title: Pick the eye for the job
muc.text: Notice how they choose: a camera to read text, radar to measure speed in any weather, LiDAR to avoid people precisely. Wherever someone could get hurt, combine two or more kinds.

muc.title: The parking lot exercise
muc.text: A parking lot wants to count free spaces and read the plates of cars entering the gate. Choose a sensor for each job yourself, then check the answer in the pinned comment.
